C10 and C22 share much of the same recurring Citizenship Day formulation but are less proximate than C20, which concerns the same September 17, 1956 observance.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"One hundred and sixty-nine years ago today, on Monday, September 17, 1787, the Constitution of the United States was signed","parent_excerpt":"the 17th day of September of each year as Citizenship Day in commemoration of the signing of the Constitution of the United States on September 17, 1787","explanation":"Both frame the observance around the identical constitutional anniversary and historical event."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby urge the Governors of the several States, and do call upon all officials and agencies of Federal Government, and upon all citizens, to observe ... with appropriate activities and ceremonies","parent_excerpt":"do call upon the appropriate officials of the Government ... I also urge Federal, State, and local officials ... to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day","explanation":"The child follows the parent's operative pattern of calling upon officials and the public to conduct an appropriate commemorative observance."},{"child_excerpt":"I hereby direct that on January 11, 1957 ... the flag of the United States be appropriately displayed on all Government buildings","parent_excerpt":"do call upon the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on Monday, September 17, 1956","explanation":"This is concrete shared administrative machinery and closely parallel language, with the child substituting Hamilton's birthday for Citizenship Day."}]}
